title: FAR Module 2 · TBS 3

fields.label: 4. Increase in Expense From the Inventory Write-Down

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Inventory Ownership & Valuation

Determine the inventory owned at year-end and apply the appropriate valuation adjustment.

Scenario

Redwood Corp. uses the FIFO inventory method. At December 31, Redwood's physical inventory count totaled $310,000.

The following items require analysis:

  • The physical count includes $18,000 of merchandise held by Redwood on consignment for another company.
  • Merchandise costing $24,000 was purchased FOB shipping point and shipped to Redwood on December 29. The goods were still in transit at December 31 and were not included in the physical count.
  • Merchandise costing $15,000 was sold by Redwood FOB destination on December 30. The customer received the goods on January 3. The goods were not included in Redwood's physical count.

Valuation Information

After correcting the inventory ownership items above, Redwood determines that one group of inventory has:

Cost $80,000
Net Realizable Value $73,000

Assume the remaining inventory has net realizable value at or above cost and requires no write-down.

Required

1. Inventory Owned Before Valuation Adjustment
2. Inventory Write-Down
3. Final Reported Inventory
4. Increase in Expense From the Inventory Write-Down
explanation:
Step 1 — Correct the Physical Count

Start with the physical inventory count:

$310,000

The $18,000 of consigned merchandise belongs to another company, so Redwood must exclude it.

$310,000 − $18,000 = $292,000

The $24,000 purchase was shipped FOB shipping point. Ownership passed to Redwood when the seller shipped the goods, so it must be included.

$292,000 + $24,000 = $316,000

The $15,000 sale was shipped FOB destination. Because the customer had not yet received the goods at December 31, Redwood still owned them.

$316,000 + $15,000 = $331,000

Inventory Owned Before Valuation: $331,000

Step 2 — Apply Lower of Cost and NRV

The affected inventory has cost of $80,000 and net realizable value of $73,000.

$80,000 − $73,000 = $7,000 Write-Down

Inventory Write-Down: $7,000

Step 3 — Final Inventory

$331,000 − $7,000 = $324,000

Final Reported Inventory: $324,000

Step 4 — Income Statement Effect

The $7,000 inventory write-down creates a $7,000 loss or expense, reducing current-period income.

Increase in Expense: $7,000

CPA Takeaway

  • Consigned goods belong to the consignor, not the consignee.
  • FOB shipping point generally transfers ownership when goods are shipped.
  • FOB destination generally transfers ownership when the buyer receives the goods.
  • For this FIFO inventory, when NRV falls below cost, inventory is written down to NRV.
